ruling.recommended_action: Reject the rider's claim on the agreed Halus Link detour (covered by RD-5 consent), but refund the unconsented U-turn loop on the Tampines Expressway / Tampines Ave 10 (~1.30 km) plus its ERP-type overcharge, as a voucher per NS-7.

segment_findings.reason: Driver asked in writing BEFORE the deviation ('Traffic ahead on Tampines Expressway is building up, ok if I go round via Halus Link?', 10:01:00) and the rider's own message agreed ('Sure, go ahead.', 10:01:40), before the off-route trace begins at 10:01:50; the agreed content covers exactly this turn-off. RD-5 (with RD-3(a)) → no_action for this segment; added distance is at most ~0.3 km.

Unrequested U-turn/overshoot on the Tampines Expressway corridor (~10:02:50 → 10:05:50, overshooting the correct exit at ~1.3850,103.9183 and returning NE ~1.3 km). It is separate from the consented Halus Link turn, there is no prior chat covering it and no RD-4 incident on record (TEX band 4, weather Fair) → not exempt under RD-1/RD-3/RD-4/RD-5; refund under RD-2 (non-metered branch) computed on ~1.30 km × SGD 1.41/km ≈ SGD 1.83.

rejected_claims.reason: The complaint claims the whole 'longer way round' was unauthorised and overcharged. The chat shows the rider personally agreed in writing, before the turn-off, to go round via Halus Link; under RD-5 that segment is exempt, so only the subsequent U-turn loop is refundable.
